outcomes.statement: describes the elements and principles of design and uses them in a variety of applications
identifies the functional and aesthetic requirements and features of a range of textile items
demonstrates the use of a variety of communication skills, including computer-based technology
develops competence in the selection and use of appropriate manufacturing techniques and equipment
manages the design and manufacture of textile projects
identifies properties of a variety of fabrics, yarns and fibres
justifies the selection of fabrics, yarns and fibres for end-uses
identifies and selects textiles for specific end-uses based on analysis of experimentation
examines the status of the Australian Textile, Clothing, Footwear and Allied Industries within the global context
investigates the range of career options in design, consumerism, manufacturing and retail sectors of the Australian Textile, Clothing, Footwear and Allied Industries
identifies and appreciates the factors that contribute to the quality and value of textiles in society
critically analyses and explains the factors that have contributed to the design and manufacture of the Major Textiles Project
designs a textile item or items that demonstrates an understanding of functional and aesthetic requirements
identifies the principles of colouration for specific end-uses
communicates design concepts and manufacturing specifications to both technical and non-technical audiences
demonstrates proficiency in the manufacture of a textile item or items
effectively manages the design and manufacture of a Major Textiles Project to completion
explains the interrelationship between fabric, yarn and fibre properties
develops knowledge and awareness of emerging textile technologies
justifies the selection of fabric, yarn, fibre and fabric finishing techniques for specific end-uses
selects and justifies manufacturing techniques, materials and equipment for a specific end-use
investigates and describes aspects of marketing in the textile industry
analyses and discusses the impact of current issues on the Australian textiles industry
analyses the influence of historical, cultural and contemporary developments on textiles

periods.student_work: Teach Module 1 section 'Design purpose, users and requirements'; students view the design lens and complete the 10-question check.
periods.evidence: Saved written response and Folio Card 1; P1.2
syllabus_content: Functional and aesthetic design; user, purpose, context and factors determining appropriate design.

periods.student_work: Teach 'Elements of design'; model evidence-based analysis; students complete the video prompt and 10-question check.
periods.evidence: Written analysis and Folio Card 2; P1.1
syllabus_content: Line/direction, shape/size, texture, colour/value applied across textile applications.

periods.student_work: Teach 'Principles of design'; compare examples; students complete the video prompt and 10-question check.
periods.evidence: Supported judgement and Folio Card 2; P1.1
syllabus_content: Proportion, balance, rhythm, emphasis, contrast/harmony and unity.

periods.student_work: Model the Design-analysis studio. Students analyse one textile item, improve the response and save the evidence.
periods.evidence: Completed activity plus Folio Cards 1-2; P1.1, P1.2
syllabus_content: Describe and analyse elements and principles; identify functional and aesthetic requirements.

periods.student_work: Teach with the completed Module 2 theory, checks and applied-practice activity.
syllabus_content: Functional and aesthetic design across apparel, furnishings, costume, textile arts and non-apparel.

periods.student_work: Model how environmental sustainability and manufacturing techniques shape a design response.
syllabus_content: Factors determining appropriate design; role of design in meeting functional and aesthetic requirements.

periods.student_work: Students compare inspiration sources and explain how a concept changes through feedback and constraints.
syllabus_content: Generate, communicate, select and evaluate design ideas for a Preliminary textile project.

periods.student_work: Students record the user, purpose, requirements and one developed design direction in Folio Card 3.
periods.evidence: Folio Card 3 checkpoint; P1.1, P1.2, P2.1
syllabus_content: Apply elements and principles; select, analyse and record design idea development.

periods.student_work: Teacher explains approved pattern information, symbols, measurements and quality checkpoints; use the completed site module.
syllabus_content: Manufacturing methods; interpret, use and modify patterns for specific end-uses.

periods.student_work: Students prepare a teacher-approved order of work and quality checkpoints without inventing technical details.
periods.evidence: Approved plan and Folio Card 3; P2.1, P2.3
syllabus_content: Outline and justify project development and management steps; communicate production information.

periods.student_work: Teacher demonstrates the authorised technique and controls. Students practise under supervision and retain one labelled sample.
syllabus_content: Select and use manufacturing techniques appropriate to fabric and end-use.

periods.student_work: Students repeat or extend an authorised technique, check quality and record one improvement.
periods.evidence: Improved sample and feedback record; P2.2, P2.3
syllabus_content: Develop competence with appropriate manufacturing techniques and equipment.

periods.student_work: Teacher models object, fashion and production drawing conventions from authorised course sources.
syllabus_content: Graphical communication: object, fashion and industry production drawing specifications.

periods.student_work: Compare verbal, written, graphical and digital methods; students select a method for a defined audience.
syllabus_content: Criteria for effective verbal and written communication; communication-based technologies.

periods.student_work: Students create a teacher-approved drawing or annotated specification for Project 1.
periods.evidence: Communication evidence in Folio Card 3; P2.1
syllabus_content: Develop competence in graphically communicating design ideas using appropriate media.

periods.student_work: Run a short peer/teacher review. Students document one supported change and update their project plan.
syllabus_content: Communicate, evaluate and modify design ideas; manage time and resources.

periods.student_work: Check approved brief, design evidence, pattern, resources and sequence. Students identify the next authorised action.
syllabus_content: Manage project development; evaluate ideas; plan time and resources.

periods.student_work: Teacher demonstrates the approved stage. Students manufacture under supervision and complete clean-down.
periods.evidence: Progress photo/sample and teacher checkpoint; P2.2, P2.3
syllabus_content: Project construction using appropriate methods, techniques and equipment.

periods.student_work: Students continue the approved sequence, check accuracy and respond to feedback.
periods.evidence: Technique evidence in Folio Card 4; P2.2, P2.3
syllabus_content: Apply manipulative skills and manage the textile project.

periods.student_work: Students continue the approved sequence and record one quality issue or decision.
syllabus_content: Use appropriate manufacturing techniques; manage time and resources.

periods.student_work: Students complete the approved construction sequence and carry out teacher-directed quality checks.
syllabus_content: Complete and evaluate a Preliminary textile project using appropriate methods.

periods.student_work: Students photograph the authorised result, compare it with requirements and record a realistic improvement.
periods.evidence: Folio Card 6 evaluation; P1.2, P2.3, P4.1
syllabus_content: Evaluate ideas and project; substantiate conclusions with factual evidence.

periods.student_work: Teacher-led classification lesson using the approved properties booklet; use the completed site module.
syllabus_content: Natural, regenerated and synthetic fibre types and classifications.

periods.student_work: Explain monomer, polymer, amorphous and crystalline regions with verified diagrams.
syllabus_content: Molecular structure and its contribution to fibre properties.

periods.student_work: Compare surface and cross-sectional features, staple, filament and multifilament forms.
syllabus_content: Morphological structure and its contribution to fibre properties.

periods.student_work: Students choose one verified fibre example and justify an end use using structure and properties.
syllabus_content: Select fibres for specific end-uses using evidence about properties.

periods.student_work: Teach cotton origin, structure, processing, properties and end-use from approved sources.
syllabus_content: Properties of natural cellulosic fibre; cotton classification and performance.

periods.student_work: Teach wool origin, structure, processing, properties and end-use from approved sources.
syllabus_content: Properties of natural protein fibre; wool classification and performance.

periods.student_work: Compare viscose rayon, polyester, nylon, elastomeric and the required blends.
syllabus_content: At least one regenerated, three synthetic fibres and two fibre blends.

periods.student_work: Students justify one natural and one manufactured fibre or blend for contrasting end uses.
syllabus_content: Describe fibre properties and justify fibre selection for end-use.

periods.student_work: Compare staple-spun and filament construction and apply correct terminology.
syllabus_content: Spun staple and filament yarn structure and characteristics.

periods.student_work: Explain low/high twist and carded/combed or woollen/worsted distinctions.
syllabus_content: Twist level and spinning systems that affect yarn and fabric properties.

periods.student_work: Identify textured, slub, boucle and core-spun examples from verified sources or teacher samples.
syllabus_content: Textured and novelty yarn structures and characteristics.

periods.student_work: Students select one yarn structure and explain how it contributes to fabric behaviour.
periods.evidence: Folio Card 7 yarn record; P3.1, P3.2
syllabus_content: Identify yarn characteristics that affect fabric properties.

periods.student_work: Teach how yarn structure affects appearance, handle and comfort.
syllabus_content: Yarn aesthetic and comfort properties and their effect on fabric performance.

periods.student_work: Compare durability, strength and care demands using verified examples.
syllabus_content: Yarn durability, strength and care properties.

periods.student_work: Model a chain from fibre to yarn structure to fabric performance and end use.
syllabus_content: Interrelationship of yarn structure, yarn properties and fabric performance.

periods.student_work: Students justify a yarn selection for a specific textile end use using evidence.
syllabus_content: Demonstrate understanding of yarn properties when selecting fabrics for end-use.

periods.student_work: Teach warp, weft and selvedge, then compare plain, twill, satin, Jacquard, crepe and pile weaves.
syllabus_content: Woven fabric structure, terminology, types and classification.

periods.student_work: Teach course and wale, then compare the required knitted fabric types.
syllabus_content: Single, double, tricot, pile, lace and net knitted structures.

periods.student_work: Compare felt, web and film structures and link construction to likely performance.
syllabus_content: Non-woven fabric structures, classification and properties.

periods.student_work: Using teacher-approved samples and method, students identify structure and record evidence rather than appearance alone.
periods.evidence: Folio Card 7 sample record; P3.1, P3.2
syllabus_content: Identify fabric structures and describe properties affected by structure.

periods.student_work: Compare aesthetic, durability, comfort, dimensional stability and care properties.
syllabus_content: Fabric and fibre properties used when selecting fabrics for specific end-uses.

periods.student_work: Model an aim, variables, consistent method, results table and evidence-based conclusion without supplying an unapproved method.
syllabus_content: Use functional and aesthetic tests to record and evaluate results.

periods.student_work: Students prepare Folio Card 8 fields and a teacher-approved recording format before testing.
syllabus_content: Plan experimental procedures; communicate and record information.

periods.student_work: Teacher demonstrates the approved method and controls. Students test, record results and clean down under supervision.
periods.evidence: Results and observations in Folio Card 8; P3.1, P4.1
syllabus_content: Evaluate fabric properties using classroom testing procedures.

periods.student_work: Students analyse authorised test results and justify one fabric, yarn or fibre selection for the confirmed project.
syllabus_content: Make decisions about textiles using analysis of properties and experimental evidence.

periods.student_work: Teacher demonstrates the approved Bustier/Vest stage. Students work under supervision and complete clean-down.
syllabus_content: Project 2 construction using techniques appropriate to fabric and end-use.

periods.student_work: Students continue the approved sequence, check quality and record a supported decision.
periods.evidence: Teacher checkpoint and Folio Card 9; P2.1, P2.2, P2.3
syllabus_content: Apply manipulative and management skills; communicate and record information.

periods.student_work: Students complete the authorised item, collect product evidence and evaluate design, selection and manufacture.
periods.evidence: Completed Folio Card 9; P2.3, P3.2, P4.1
syllabus_content: Evaluate textile selection and project outcomes using factual evidence.

periods.student_work: Use current primary evidence to outline one ATCFAI sector and its development; use the completed site module.
syllabus_content: Role of textiles; sectors; development across the 19th, 20th and 21st centuries.

periods.student_work: Compare Australian industry participation with global markets and identify one current issue using dated sources.
syllabus_content: Contribution to local/global markets; issues, trends and future opportunities.

periods.student_work: Students investigate one current career pathway, required training and changing work context.
periods.evidence: Career profile for Folio Card 10; P5.2
syllabus_content: Current and future employment and training opportunities across ATCFAI sectors.

periods.student_work: Compare design, trademarks, fabric quality, legislation, assurance checks and control measures.
syllabus_content: Influences on quality; methods of quality assurance in the marketplace.

periods.student_work: Examine manufacturer/consumer roles and perceived, cultural and economic value.
syllabus_content: Factors contributing to quality and value across textile end-uses.

periods.student_work: Students build one sourced case analysis and record title, organisation, date and location.
syllabus_content: Investigate quality assurance and discuss factors contributing to textile value.

periods.student_work: Retrieve Design concepts, diagnose gaps and plan one supported response using command terms.
periods.evidence: Low-stakes check and response plan; P1.1-P2.3
syllabus_content: Design content from elements/principles through communication, manufacture and Project 1.

periods.student_work: Retrieve fibre, yarn, fabric, testing and selection concepts; correct misconceptions.
periods.evidence: Low-stakes check and response plan; P3.1, P3.2, P4.1
syllabus_content: Properties and Performance content; experimentation and end-use selection.

periods.student_work: Students connect design, textile performance and industry/value in unfamiliar examples.
syllabus_content: Integrated application of the three Preliminary areas of study.

periods.student_work: Students check Folio Cards 1-10, identify incomplete evidence and prepare a personal revision priority list.
periods.evidence: Folio completeness record and next-step plan; P1.1-P6.1
syllabus_content: Evaluate and communicate project, experimental and industry evidence across the course.

periods.student_work: Use Module 1 to distinguish Preliminary foundations from HSC applications. Students map the four HSC components and write one personal retrieval priority.
syllabus_content: HSC course structure; continuity from Preliminary Design, Properties and industry learning; the MTP as a distinct HSC requirement.

periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students collate authorised initial evidence, identify gaps and create a bounded next-action plan. Teacher approval, equipment access and local WHS controls remain explicit checkpoints.
syllabus_content: Management of design and manufacture; communication of initial concepts; local project approval boundaries.
periods.evidence: Initial evidence inventory and next-action plan; H2.1, H2.3
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.focus: Tracing one focus area over time
periods.student_work: Teach students to build a selective historical timeline using dated, attributable evidence rather than a list of fashions. Compare changes in silhouette, materials, manufacture and use.
syllabus_content: Historical design development within one focus area; evidence of change over time.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Model a cause-and-effect chain linking social, economic, technological, political and cultural factors to specific design decisions.
syllabus_content: Factors contributing to historical textile design and manufacture; influence on design development.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students move from description to analysis by connecting a source, a design feature, the factor that shaped it and its consequence. They identify one defensible influence for their own project.
syllabus_content: Analysis of historical developments; application of influence to MTP design reasoning.
periods.evidence: One structured historical analysis and MTP influence note; H1.1, H6.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students document how a historical influence changes function, form, material or construction in their concept. They distinguish transformation from superficial copying.
syllabus_content: Historical influence on the design and manufacture of the MTP; communication of design development.
periods.evidence: Before/after concept annotation; H1.1, H1.2, H2.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Investigate the current teacher-selected designer or approved WWHS case study. Students separate observable design characteristics from unsupported claims about intention.
syllabus_content: Contemporary designer practice, sources of inspiration and distinguishing design characteristics.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Classify factors within and beyond a designer's organisation, then evaluate how two factors affect design, production or market success.
syllabus_content: Internal and external factors contributing to the success of a contemporary designer.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Use dated examples to test whether a designer follows, adapts or shapes a trend. Students identify one contemporary influence that can be justified in their MTP rather than merely named.
syllabus_content: Relationship between contemporary designers and trends; application to personal design development.
periods.evidence: Trend relationship paragraph and MTP influence record; H1.1, H6.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students refine one concept through a contemporary influence while retaining their own brief, user and purpose. Record the design decision and the evidence supporting it.
syllabus_content: Factors contributing to MTP design; visual development and communication of concepts.
periods.evidence: Refined concept plus evidence-based annotation; H1.1, H1.2, H2.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.focus: Colour principles for specific end use
periods.student_work: Retrieve colour relationships, contrast, harmony, value and intensity. Students justify a colour direction by linking visual effect, user, function and context.
syllabus_content: Principles of colouration and selection of colour for specific end uses.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Compare selected printing and dyeing processes by where colour is applied, the required control and the likely result. Local chemical, equipment and WHS procedures are teacher-directed.
syllabus_content: Principles and processes of fabric colouration through printing and dyeing.
periods.evidence: Process comparison with end-use judgement; H1.3, H4.2
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Model a fair sample plan with one purposeful variable, consistent controls, labelled observations and an end-use criterion. Students draft a teacher-approvable method.
syllabus_content: Experimentation with colouration methods; selection for a specific end use.
periods.evidence: Approved sample plan and predicted criterion; H1.3, H4.2
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Under teacher direction, students produce or analyse an authorised colouration sample, record actual evidence and decide whether it suits the MTP. No site instruction substitutes for local WHS controls.
syllabus_content: Application and evaluation of colouration in the design and manufacture of the MTP.
periods.evidence: Labelled sample, observation and justified decision; H1.3, H4.2
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Compare how selected decoration techniques attach, build or alter a surface. Link visual effect and structural consequence to the intended end use.
syllabus_content: Principles and use of applique, embroidery and other surface-decoration processes.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students analyse accuracy, control, repeatability, time, equipment and surface effect to choose between hand and machine approaches for a defined purpose.
syllabus_content: Selection of decoration techniques, materials and equipment for a specific end use.
periods.evidence: Decision matrix and written justification; H4.2
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students follow the teacher-approved process, make comparable samples and record material, setting, sequence and observed result. Equipment access and WHS remain local teacher controls.
syllabus_content: Experimentation and proficiency in manufacturing techniques relevant to the MTP.
periods.evidence: Labelled samples and process record; H2.2, H4.2
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.focus: Comparing samples and selecting a method
periods.student_work: Use functional, aesthetic and production criteria to compare samples. Students retain rejected evidence and justify the selected or revised technique.
syllabus_content: Evaluation of techniques and materials for MTP design and manufacture.
periods.evidence: Comparative evaluation and MTP technique decision; H1.1, H4.2
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Introduce the WWHS Hmong culture study through sourced context and careful language. Students distinguish evidence, inference and generalisation, recognising diversity within communities.
syllabus_content: Cultural factors influencing textile design and production; textiles as forms of cultural expression.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students examine how location, available resources, skill, social context and processes can shape textile production. They record what is known and what must not be assumed.
syllabus_content: Relationship of cultural context, resources, skills and production processes to textile forms.
periods.evidence: Evidence map with uncertainty labels; H1.1, H6.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Model respectful influence through transferable design principles such as labour, layering, contrast or narrative structure—not copying culturally significant motifs. Students test one concept against this boundary.
syllabus_content: Cultural influence on design; ethical and respectful development of an individual MTP.
periods.evidence: Respectful-influence rationale and revised concept; H1.1, H1.2, H6.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students audit citations, image permissions, captions and wording in their influence evidence. Unsupported cultural claims are removed or marked for teacher confirmation.
syllabus_content: Communication and management of source-grounded MTP design development.
periods.evidence: Cultural-evidence audit and next action; H2.1, H2.3, H6.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.focus: Generating ideas and selecting a direction
periods.student_work: Generate meaningfully different ideas from the brief, then use explicit functional, aesthetic and feasibility criteria to select and defend a final direction.
syllabus_content: Visual design development, creativity and innovation in the MTP.
periods.evidence: Idea range, selection matrix and decision; H1.1, H1.2, H2.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students unpack user, purpose, performance, comfort, appearance, style and context, then convert each requirement into a design response that can be observed or tested.
syllabus_content: Functional and aesthetic requirements of the MTP.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Develop production drawings and technical/non-technical specifications suited to the project. Include only project-relevant dimensions, materials, notions and sequencing.
syllabus_content: Communication of design concepts and manufacturing specifications.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students convert the approved manufacture sequence into a living plan with dependencies, checkpoints and contingency actions. Current school milestones remain teacher-confirmed.
syllabus_content: Management of design and manufacture to completion.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.focus: Building a fair and useful investigation
periods.student_work: Frame an investigation around an actual MTP decision. Define an aim, one purposeful variable, controls, a repeatable method and decision criteria for teacher approval.
syllabus_content: Investigation and experimentation supporting material, technique and process selection.
periods.evidence: Teacher-approvable investigation plan; H1.1, H4.1, H4.2
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Under local teacher direction, produce or analyse authorised samples. Record what occurred using photographs, labels, measurements or precise observations without back-filling an expected result.
syllabus_content: Accurate communication of experimentation and manufacturing evidence.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Compare evidence with the stated criteria, identify limitations and make a specific keep/change/reject decision. Link the decision to the brief and end use.
syllabus_content: Evaluation of experimentation and its contribution to MTP design and manufacture.
periods.evidence: Evidence-based design-change record; H1.1, H4.1, H4.2
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students check that each experiment has a decision purpose, method, authentic evidence, evaluation and visible consequence. Plan the smallest remaining investigation.
syllabus_content: Management and communication of MTP investigation evidence.
periods.evidence: Experimentation audit and next investigation; H2.1, H2.3
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Distinguish invention, innovation and improvement. Analyse how performance needs, resource constraints, markets, research and social priorities can drive textile change.
syllabus_content: Nature and development of textile innovations and emerging technologies.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Compare current source-verified examples at fibre, yarn and fabric level. Trace how a structural change is intended to alter performance.
syllabus_content: Innovations in fibres, yarns and fabrics and their emerging applications.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Evaluate an innovation from consumer, manufacturer, employee and environmental viewpoints. Students identify an MTP-relevant possibility but avoid unsupported novelty claims.
syllabus_content: Impacts of textile innovations on products, processes, people and environment.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students investigate whether one emerging material or process is feasible and appropriate for their actual end use, resources and evidence needs. Record use, rejection or teacher-confirmation status.
syllabus_content: Selection and justification of materials, processes and equipment for the MTP.
periods.evidence: Feasibility and end-use decision; H1.1, H4.1, H4.2
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.focus: Microfibres, bicomponent yarns and washable webs
periods.student_work: Teach the specified innovation types through structure, manufacture, claimed performance and end use. Students avoid treating every fine fibre or non-woven as the same technology.
syllabus_content: Microfibres, bicomponent yarns and washable webs as textile innovations.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Retrieve Preliminary fibre, yarn and fabric knowledge, then diagnose weak links in a structure-to-property explanation before applying it to an HSC innovation.
syllabus_content: Interrelationship of fibre, yarn and fabric properties; continuity from Preliminary learning.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Start with an end-use requirement, identify the required property, connect it to structure and compare trade-offs. Apply the reasoning to one provisional MTP material.
syllabus_content: Selection of textiles for performance in specific end uses.
periods.evidence: End-use comparison and provisional selection; H3.1, H4.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students verify fibre, yarn, fabric and finish information for selected materials and identify evidence gaps. Unsupported retail claims are not used as proof.
syllabus_content: Justification of textile selection for MTP functional and aesthetic requirements.
periods.evidence: Material evidence card and next test/source; H1.1, H4.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Compare how selected production machinery and computer-supported systems change precision, speed, repeatability, labour or design communication. Use current examples only when source-verified.
syllabus_content: Developments in textile machinery and computer-supported production.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Analyse how removing or relocating seams alters production, fit, comfort, waste and design possibilities. Students distinguish a seamless process from simply hiding seams.
syllabus_content: Seamless technology and its effect on textile manufacture and performance.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Under teacher direction, compare an authorised conventional and technology-supported enhancement pathway or sample. Evaluate the result against accuracy, time, surface effect and end use.
syllabus_content: Use of machinery and decorative technologies to enhance textile products.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students justify the selected equipment and manufacturing sequence for one MTP stage, including constraints, quality controls and an approved alternative if access changes.
syllabus_content: Selection and justification of manufacturing techniques, materials and equipment for the MTP.
periods.evidence: Technology decision and contingency; H2.3, H4.2
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Translate a use scenario into observable functional and aesthetic criteria before selecting a textile. Compare how priorities shift across two focus areas.
syllabus_content: Functional and aesthetic performance criteria for textile end uses.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Compare selected finishes by treatment, intended effect, limitations and care implications. Avoid absolute performance claims unless supported by a current source.
syllabus_content: Fabric finishing techniques, performance enhancement and care requirements.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Build a full justification from fibre properties through yarn and fabric structure to finish, end-use performance and trade-offs.
syllabus_content: Interrelationship of fibre, yarn, fabric and finish in selection for specific end uses.
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students plan and write a supported response using an unfamiliar end-use scenario. Diagnose whether each sentence identifies, explains or justifies as required.
syllabus_content: Integrated Properties and Performance content applied to HSC-style questions.
periods.evidence: Timed formative response and feedback; H3.1, H3.2, H4.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.module_title: The Australian Textiles Industry and Marketplace
periods.student_work: Map key Australian textiles, clothing, footwear and allied-industry sectors and the relationships among design, supply, manufacture, retail, service and end users. Current figures require dated primary sources.
syllabus_content: Structure and sectors of the Australian textile industry and their relationships.
area_hours: Australian Textiles, Clothing, Footwear and Allied Industries
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.module_title: The Australian Textiles Industry and Marketplace
periods.student_work: Apply product, price, place and promotion to an approved textile case. Connect target market and product life-cycle position to marketing decisions.
syllabus_content: Textile marketplace, target markets, product development, marketing mix and product life cycle.
area_hours: Australian Textiles, Clothing, Footwear and Allied Industries
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.module_title: The Australian Textiles Industry and Marketplace
periods.student_work: Analyse how global supply, consumer demand, skills and workplace decisions interact. Students identify one relevant implication for communicating their MTP as a product.
syllabus_content: Globalisation, skills, consumer demand and changing industry relationships.
periods.evidence: Relationship analysis and MTP implication; H5.1, H5.2
area_hours: Australian Textiles, Clothing, Footwear and Allied Industries
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.module_title: The Australian Textiles Industry and Marketplace
periods.focus: MTP product communication and label planning
periods.student_work: Students draft product information appropriate to user and end use, then flag every legal, fibre-content, care or school requirement that needs current teacher/source confirmation.
syllabus_content: Communication of the MTP to technical and non-technical audiences; marketplace considerations.
periods.evidence: Draft product communication with confirmation flags; H2.1, H5.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Judge whether a technology is appropriate by matching scale, skill, cost, maintenance, resource use, local context and intended benefit—not by assuming newer is better.
syllabus_content: Appropriate technology, resources, alternatives and limitations in textile production.
area_hours: Australian Textiles, Clothing, Footwear and Allied Industries
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.focus: Sustainability across a product life cycle
periods.student_work: Trace material sourcing, manufacture, distribution, use, care, repair and end-of-life. Identify burden shifting and distinguish a verified improvement from a vague green claim.
syllabus_content: Environmental sustainability, recycling, pollution and product life-cycle considerations.
area_hours: Australian Textiles, Clothing, Footwear and Allied Industries
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Use a current dated source to analyse one issue from more than one stakeholder perspective. Students connect the issue to a bounded MTP decision without claiming to solve the whole problem.
syllabus_content: Impact of current social, consumer and industry issues on the Australian textiles industry.
area_hours: Australian Textiles, Clothing, Footwear and Allied Industries
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students evaluate one material, process or care decision across the relevant life-cycle stages and record a practical keep/change/mitigate action.
syllabus_content: Factors contributing to MTP design and manufacture; justified material/process choices.
periods.evidence: Bounded sustainability evaluation; H1.1, H4.1, H4.2
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Students reconcile the approved item or items, supporting-documentation evidence and remaining teacher-confirmed submission actions. The site does not certify completeness or replace official checks.
syllabus_content: Completion and management of MTP design and manufacture; communication of evidence.
periods.evidence: Completion audit and teacher-check list; H1.1, H2.1, H2.2, H2.3
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Retrieve design content while practising analyse, explain, justify and evaluate. Students annotate one plan to show where evidence, relationships and judgement will appear.
syllabus_content: Design content integrated through HSC response planning; MTP factors and influences.
periods.evidence: Annotated response plan and MTP reflection; H1.1, H1.2, H1.3, H6.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Retrieve structure-property, innovation, finish and end-use selection concepts. Students correct one misconception before completing a timed formative response.
syllabus_content: Integrated Properties and Performance content for HSC preparation.
periods.evidence: Corrected reasoning chain and timed response; H3.1, H3.2, H4.1
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm

periods.student_work: Connect marketing and current issues to an unfamiliar textile case, then build a personal revision plan across Design, Properties, industry and MTP learning. Current examination logistics remain teacher-confirmed.
syllabus_content: Integrated application of HSC Areas of Study and course outcomes.
periods.evidence: Industry response plus evidence-based revision plan; H5.1, H5.2
area_hours: Australian Textiles, Clothing, Footwear and Allied Industries
periods.assessment_status: formative learning evidence; current formal task notice Teacher to confirm
